notes.title: The Life and Suffering of Prince Jerian — a new narrative RPG from Schisma Games
notes.content:
It is our pleasure to announce a new narrative roleplay adventure from the minds behind [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1272160/The_Life_and_Suffering_of_Sir_Brante/]The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante[/url]!

The Life and Suffering of Prince Jerian is a narrative roleplaying game that casts the player as the heir to the Blessed Arknian Empire, who must carve out a destiny for his nation. The world is grim, and the gods are eager to punish anyone who breaks their commandments. People live preordained lives, their fates sealed the moment they are born. It is up to the player to decide what kind of leader they will be: uphold the established order, or build a new kind of future.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2936290/The_Life_and_Suffering_of_Prince_Jerian/

You, Prince Jerian of House Tempest, must embark on a lifelong journey. It starts in your childhood, blissfully ignorant of your destiny, and continues into maturity as you take up a role you have been primed for since birth: emperor. As crown prince, you must not only understand your country and its culture, but also make many difficult choices that affect the fragile balance of powers in the Empire, and inside yourself. If you go where political circumstance and family obligations guide you, you risk losing yourself in the chaos. Can you keep yourself whole, or will you shatter?

Check out the trailer, which will give you some first impressions about the upcoming game!

[previewyoutube=LsJb0TVRytc;full][/previewyoutube]

In addition, to celebrate the official announcement of the game, we are releasing a special video address from the development team at Schisma Games, in which they will pull back the veil of mystery shrouding the contents of their upcoming title. Come watch!

[previewyoutube=RdUQLk17Vqo;full][/previewyoutube]

The game is currently in development. Wishlist The Life and Suffering of Prince Jerian now and subscribe to our newsletter to never miss an update!

notes.title: A new story-driven game from the creators of For the People.
notes.content:
Greetings, friends!

Today is the anniversary of the release of the official simulator [b]For the People[/b], our first game. And to celebrate this day, we've prepared a new announcement for you - the debut project of [i]Dark Citadel[/i], an experimental and until recently terribly secretive division of [i]Brezg Studio[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/fac6a97ff67459a4ed56c88347d119405c6c1e6c.png[/img]

So, meet [b]True Magician[/b]. It's a non-linear narrative game with RPG elements in the vein of [i]Sorcery![/i] and [i]Choice of Magics[/i], with a story about the rise of a young apprentice wizard named Aidan. Here ancient secrets intertwine with the intrigues of the king's court, danger lurks where you least expect it, and magic grants its adherents incredible abilities - or destroys them irrevocably.

Together with Aidan you will go through many trials, discover his true potential, master the forbidden magic of the Void - and become a true wizard! Of course, if his witchcraft doesn't attract the attention of Those whose voices come from the other world...

True Magician[/b] is an interactive adventure in the best traditions of text quests: the story branches depending on the choice of the player, the world reacts to his decisions, and important characters can become enemies, friends or even more than friends... We added elements from RPG to the classic formula - combat system, inventory and development of magical skills. In addition, specially for the game was drawn art - a relatively uncommon guest in text games.

In the future we will reveal a lot of interesting things about our new project and its inhabitants. There will definitely be a demo-version to give you a closer look at the game - the exact date will be announced later. In the meantime, add [b]True Magician[/b] to your Steam wishlist, so you won't miss anything!

notes.title: For the People 1.1.3 update — full patch notes
notes.content:
We have spent the last week improving For the People and are ready to deploy another patch to make your gaming experience a breeze! The patch will be released today for all versions of the game.

Many players pointed out certain imperfections in agent missions, so we have revamped the agent appointing algorithm and added quite a bit of new content while we were at it. Here’s a shortlist of the main changes:

[list]
[*] Whereas before an agent's skills played a pivotal role in whether they were suitable for a mission, now more emphasis should be put on the individual agent's background.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Agents’ dossiers were slightly adjusted and simplified so that the player can make a decision regarding an agent faster.
[/list]
[list]
[*] We also revised the outcomes of most missions when it comes to agent failures - the descriptions will now be more definitive and detailed.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Repetitive paragraphs in the agent mission descriptions and some of the mission outcomes have been removed.
[/list]
[list]
[*] One of the repetitive citizen appeals, written by an old man complaining about the noise, can potentially affect the ending of the game.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Achievements connected to the individual districts’ opinion of the City Committee and citizen happiness will now be somewhat easier to unlock.
[/list]

Important notice: changes made to the agents will only be applied when starting a new game and will not affect existing progress.

We hope that these changes will make your gaming experience even more pleasant. As always, please continue to give us your feedback about specific For the People cases that feel excessive in this topic on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1146600/discussions/0/4325098189133146829/]Steam[/url] or in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?url=https://discord.gg/h9g48vy]Discord[/url]. Thank you for your reports and patience!

notes.title: For the People: Only two days left before the official launch!
notes.content:
That was a long journey but we made it to the final stretch! [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] launches in less than two days on the 13th of August and we would like to share some information regarding the latest updates and improvements that were made to the game.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/

First and foremost - we couldn't be more grateful to our amazingly supportive community! It was an absolute blessing to get so many insightful reviews and helpful feedback from our Comrades. The team surely wouldn't be able to get this far without you!

Now let's take a closer look at the changes we made and the new features that were implemented to facilitate your enjoyment of our newest title. Those who have previously played the demo will no doubt immediately spot the difference between it and the latest version of the game. We hope you'll like it! 


[b][h3]In-game hints[/h3][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/9ea5d6446e09976b9a81049893c62eaafb825f21.gif[/img]

Some users suggested implementing a system of hints that will help newcomers during their first playthrough by explaining in-game events and mechanics in greater detail. You asked for it and we have delivered - hovering the mouse cursor over certain elements of the game’s interface will now display popups with a short explanation of what these items are and how to use them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/9df25765f8783e950751a3560fdc2d25d106a65e.gif[/img]


[b][h3]Save/Load menu[/h3][/b]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] includes more than five alternate endings, so if you’re aiming to arrive at a specific conclusion to the story it's generally recommended to save your progress as often as possible - many of the player’s decisions will have serious, sometimes unforeseen consequences and may potentially alter the course of in-game history!

Don't worry though - we got you covered! Multiple additional slots have been added to the save/load menu so that you don't need to worry about missing any opportunities - simply go back in time and relive the same moment again, ultimately making a different choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/b3a86268e98d932e10d9a00a81845a35a760ec3a.png[/img]


[h3][b]Fonts and readability[/b][/h3]

In a nutshell, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] is an interactive novel meaning there's TONS of content for the player to read through. Never losing sight of this fact, we have readjusted the size as well as other aspects of the in-game fonts in order to improve their readability and the general accessibility of our project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/c7a4652457668c9a1d2c75994afba6a2a9a9ceb4.png[/img]


[h3][b]Recourses management and budget allocation[/b][/h3]

Some of our users pointed out that the economic planning screen could be made larger, cleaner, and easier to click around in... Well, we have heard you loud and clear! The regional management menu has seen a general overhaul, sporting not only a revised visual design but also additional hints on producing and transporting resources to and from Iron-1.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/d38f1eecd07448bbe7922f694d57a8299e03aefe.gif[/img]

Public funds allocation mechanics were improved as well - instead of constantly having to keep individual districts’ needs and requests in mind or checking the status screen before making every important decision you can now simply read the reports carefully prepared by your assistant Helen!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/d364d2f98a3b958e401d40e45427ba92d8e24aad.gif[/img]


[h3][b]Lore and world-building[/b][/h3]

While working on the game, our aim was to create an alternate history scenario where the ruling Orange Party has its own goals that diverge from the interests of the “proletariat.” This confrontation is at the cornerstone of the story presented in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] and it was important to properly showcase this idea without interrupting any major game events, thus ensuring that the player can discover and explore the game’s lore at their own pace.

Should you ever feel lost or unsure about a certain term, you can now click the map hanging on the wall of Frank’s office and dive into the history of the UPOC. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/27c436edb430ccde8aa53cd93162b709ac526ebb.gif[/img]

Alternatively, click the city map right in the middle of the mayor’s desk, navigate to the Anna Tietrich City Library and learn more about the main historical events, city buildings, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/8d7763e8676eecc034f5ce48b1c18312f16361bf.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/eb8682a3141d21938e083c214d59cc387655f64a.jpg[/img]



This was just a small fraction of the changes brought on by the latest patches and updates leading up to the official Steam launch on the 13th of August.

[b]If you haven’t wishlisted and followed [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] until now we strongly recommend you to do so in order to enjoy the delightful release day discount![/b]

We would also really appreciate it if you helped us spread the word - tell your favorite YouTuber, streamer, or a gaming media outlet about the upcoming release and feel free to share this post with your friends!

notes.title: Dev diaries, part 2: Alternate history in the world of For the People
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/0e4d67192dbf5a2f7431e8f6cd244bc8349a137a.png[/img]


Today we continue a series of interviews with the team of developers behind [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] — the gallant trio of comrades from the indie studio Brezg!

A brief recap for those who have missed the previous article: in “[url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/1146600/view/2236544252825716602]Dev Diaries part one[/url]” we have discussed the challenges the studio had to face during early development, the difficulties of building a strong team, and finally answered the question of why a crucial milestone in the process of releasing a new game - finding a reliable publisher - oftentimes feels like looking for a needle in a haystack.

In the second part of this series, we’re going to find out why Iron-1 is a lookalike of the Russian city Vorkuta, what served as the starting point of For the People’s story, and how a delayed payment of pensions can change the course of history.

Answering our questions today are the studio’s co-founders Artem Murtola, Pavel Mavidi, and Nickita Birukov — lead scriptwriter and the author of the original concept.


https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/


[h3]How did you come up with the idea of the world showcased in For the People? Why did you decide to go with this exact kind of narrative and lore?[/h3]

[i]A game’s “lore” is a fusion of backstory and worldbuilding elements complementing its principal narrative.[/i]

Creating a compelling urban narrative was one of the most interesting yet challenging tasks that our scriptwriters had to face during the development process.

We were always huge fans of political and historical games, especially those where the story was set in an alternate history scenario and the player’s choices directly affected the outcome of the game as well as the protagonist’s fate.

After repeatedly playing through many of the strategy titles by Paradox Interactive (large video games developer and publisher, makers of such popular franchises as Crusader Kings, Hearts of Iron, and many others - Ed.) we decided to make a game in this genre ourselves.

That’s how the concept for an in-game universe, in many ways similar to the one we currently live in, was born. It would be perfectly suited for simulating a variety of events akin to those that happened during the real-world XX century: revolutions, world wars, economic crises, and many others, but with different results. When we later came up with the idea of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url], this setting proved to be the perfect match for the kind of game we had envisioned.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/9cadab609d045b0351c71f33c2460936a549d4fc.jpg[/img]


[h3]What was your source of inspiration while working on the game’s lore?[/h3]

While working on the prototype of Iron-1 and describing a society it existed in, we mostly relied on our own knowledge as well as numerous recollections by people who had experienced first-hand the life in Russia some half a century ago.

We had a lot of things to process — the legacy of the Soviet era encompasses movies, songs, art pieces, landmarks, and memories from the people who lived in the USSR.

We also had to study the Western culture, borrowing elements typically associated with the ’80s and trying to look at them through the prism of contemporary socialist worldview.

For instance, the noir detective questlines found in-game were mostly inspired by the famous comic series Sin City.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/5a7db70deca9d461cc7fa23f80afb821b1f170cb.png[/img]


[h3]How did you come up with the Unity of People’s Orange Communes (UPOC)? Is it also a reference to the USSR?[/h3]

Indeed it is, but it’s important not to think of UPOC and USSR as the same exact entity. Our goal was to create an alternate history scenario where the Perestroika took on a different route. The game has nothing to do with real-life politics and political organizations. Keep in mind that it’s a different fictional world.

The ruling Orange Party has its own goals which diverge from the interests of the “proletariat”. This confrontation is at the cornerstone of the story presented in For the People.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/09dc7470868a597200690042533aae7b86695ab4.jpg[/img]


[h3]How much time did it take to work out all the details of the lore?[/h3]

The part of the in-game universe we had to work on the most was figuring out its political and socio-economic structure, as well as conceptualizing the interconnected roles of the state, the Iron-1 city, its history, and inhabitants. All of that took us a better part of six months and we kept on deepening, transforming, and adding to the lore until the latest stages of development.

It was sometimes difficult to stick to a civil discussion while coming up with all of this — we argued a lot and often weren’t able to find common ground. Each member of the team suggested his or her own interpretation of the game’s events, had their own completely different vision of how the game’s story should progress (all three smile).

[h3]Is Iron-1 a real city or a fictional one? Have to admit — it looks pretty real.[/h3]

If you were lucky enough to visit some of the remote Russian cities like Surgut or Vorkuta than the environment of Iron-1 would seem instantly familiar to you (they smile).

We wanted to tell the life story of a government official ruling a small upcountry town in the middle of nowhere, that’s how we came up with the concept for a small industrial city with the name that speaks for itself — “Iron-1”.

[h3]What about the main characters of the game and especially the young mayor of Iron-1 Francis River? Did he have a real-life prototype?[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/dfd0bdc0e071be32c268c6337bf4ac32dcf84211.jpg[/img]


Surprisingly we had the least amount of questions and disagreements regarding our protagonist. Francis came to be at the very first meeting we had about our future game.

This is how it went: we have gathered at a small cafe to discuss the concept for the game and its core mechanics. The venue was located near a subway station called ‘Chernaya rechka’ which means ‘Black River’ in English. And that’s how we came up with the last name for our hero — River.

The name Frank was suggested by one of our screenwriters. Back then he was binge-watching another season of the House of Cards (an American TV show widely popular outside of the US as well), where the main character was called Frank (Francis) Underwood.

And thus Francis River was born.

[h3]As your colleagues, we have already gotten our hands on the playable demo of For the People. We noticed that it’s full of secondary and episodic characters. Are you afraid that the players might get confused at all?[/h3]

The main treasure of the glorious Iron-1 is its citizens. While we were working on For the People we tried to populate the city with realistic and believable characters. Each of them has their own personality, desires, and problems.

Each of the characters the player will encounter should add something to the story. Behind a minor bummer, such as the delayed payment of pensions, a whole new story may be hidden — sometimes funny, sometimes sad, or even outright tragic.

One way or another the majority of characters in the game can affect your decisions and their stories tend to intertwine. Some would help the player, but others, on the contrary, would throw sand into the gears of your well-oiled state machine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/72bd1e2a2a1a482428ddbb438676c357f4be9b42.png[/img]


[h3]Please tell us more about the mystery elements in the game. Frankly speaking, they are quite unusual for a simulation game. Or maybe you don’t define For the People as a typical sim game?[/h3]

We experimented with genres a lot. Perhaps adding a bit of detective fiction into the mix was not the most obvious decision according to classic gamedev conventions, but in our opinion, it will help players immerse themselves into the game’s storyline to better emphasize with the characters.

Playing a private eye in-game is like watching a murder mystery — the viewer always tries to predict the outcome. But in comparison to a lot of detective stories, For the People’s finale ain’t going to be easy to anticipate. We don’t want to hear the players say ‘I knew it from the start!’ when they have finished their playthrough.

[i]The suspect must be sent to the gallows by the player, not the screenwriter.[/i]

We have added quite a few false traces and tricky plot twists with the aim of helping the player explore the world of Francis River rather than confuse them. The game is meant to be as honest as possible with the person who plays it and we hope they will appreciate this (all three smile).

To be continued...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/714b16da74b82c394b6e2b4205bcf254d078907d.jpg[/img]


[h3]Do not miss the official release — add [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/]For the People[/url] to your wishlist now!![/h3]

notes.title: Dev diaries, part 1: The genesis of For the People
notes.content:
The release day of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1146600/For_the_People/][b]For the People[/b][/url] — the result of collaboration between 101XP and the indie studio Brezg — is drawing near. While our comrades are adding some final touches, we have taken this opportunity to peek at their monitors and ask the developers about the difficulties they ran into, important stages of game design, as well as their plans for the future.

[i]Provided below is only an excerpt from a much longer interview. We simply could not resist overwhelming the devs with questions, so stay tuned for future updates that will only get more and more interesting from this point onwards![/i]

Answering our questions today are the studio’s co-founders Artem Murtola, Pavel Mavidi, and Nickita Birukov — lead scriptwriter and the author of the original idea for the project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/fea94acb5b1135c1b6c5f90967fa0f4f8b17635b.png[/img]

[h2]How it started[/h2]
[h3]Can you tell us how the concept of For the People was born? Has it changed much during development?[/h3]
We fell in love with video games at an early age and always wanted to make games of our own. We came up with the concept for our first project way back when in 2011. It went something like this: Artem could not wait to get some coding done, Pasha wanted to write all the in-game text, and Nickita... Well, he does not quite remember what he wanted to do (all three smile), but it was ultimately he who came up with the idea of For the People.

After spending three months working on the game's concept, we were still unsure what to do with it... Back then, none of us had any experience at all. Disappointed, we threw up our arms and decided that we were simply not carved out for the gaming industry. We moved on — someone landed a good office job, everyone found new hobbies. For the time being, the dream of making a cool new game remained unfulfilled.

It took us a few years to return to the world of video games and take on the implementation of the current project with renewed strength. The fundamental idea behind it did not change, though we revised the gameplay, spicing it up with additional mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/e80bc81ba24cf4201f50abbb9ba10ec05bd2e987.png[/img]

[h3]What motivated you to go back?[/h3]
We reviewed the game's concept somewhat and decided to give it another go, recruiting the help of the only gamedev professional we knew personally — an experienced developer from the top agency — and shared one of our ideas with him. Upon receiving positive feedback, we felt inspired and immediately rushed to work on a pilot project.

[h2]About the genre[/h2]
[h3]Why have you chosen this particular setting for your story? How did you come up with the idea of combining the strategy and visual novel genres?[/h3]
Funny story: during an early meeting with our future lead developer Timophey Khakhanov, the first thing he asked was what genre we envisioned the game to fall in and received four completely different answers (they giggle in unison).

Originally, For the People more firmly resembled a typical interactive story. Now we define the game as a mix of strategy and a visual novel that focuses on acute social issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/a0013e905a8bf77ca096a64c77c4662591b94bb5.png[/img]

[h3]Newcomers to the gaming industry infamously face many problems at the start of the journey. Be frank: how many proverbial bruises did you get? Was it a challenge to assemble a team of like-minded individuals?[/h3]
Forming a team is a daunting task for any indie studio. Not only did we need to find good specialists, but they also had to be the kind of people to instantly get the feeling for everything we were trying to accomplish as well as be prepared to do the best with the limited resources at our disposal.

We put the very first team together with nothing more than bare enthusiasm and a little bit of networking — a few members were our former classmates, many others learned about our effort from mutual friends. Over time, the team line-up changed: some people burned out and lost interest, especially the guys who could only work on the project in their free time.

Six months later we ran into the first serious hurdle: due to inexperience, we severely miscalculated the time estimates and would miss several deadlines.

Though we originally planned to finish the game in the span of one year, six months later we barely had a functioning test level ready. It is funny to remember now, but back then we were crushed with disappointment, got deep into debt, and failed our first attempt miserably.

[h3]Yet you continued to work despite all that and the missed deadlines?[/h3]
Of course! This experience proved to be invaluable. We still had our small office and a team of passionate people, eyes burning with the desire to create something neat. We were ready for round two.

This time we expected to wrap up development by September 2018, but as we approached this date we realized that it would be necessary to push it further and further away. Releasing an undercooked product that did not meet our expectations would not satisfy us.

This was where our second trial awaited: people became so demoralized that they started to leave the company and there was nothing we could do about it. In the end, we decided to take a break and carefully think our situation over.

The studio was on the verge of shutting down.

[h2]The secret souce[/h2]
[h3]Very dramatic, but now For the People is getting ready for release, which means you did not give up. What is your secret?[/h3]
Perseverance! (they smile) We reassembled the team in 2019. From among the enthusiasts who helped us pave the way up until that point, only Gleb Nikonov (screenwriter and co-author), Ilya Rudnev (art director and artist), and Rauph Galautdinoff (artist and UX designer) remained. Joined by the team lead Timophey Khakhanov, we began to gradually enlist new developer talent. The localization team alone expanded to seven people. In July 2019 Elena Kabirova — our co-founder and editor — also joined the team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/570b5e4a46eff35228bcbd4044e4a51864a94611.png[/img]

[h2]The long search for a publisher[/h2]
There are many indie teams in the CIS and making a name for oneself can be very difficult. Have you been looking for a publisher for a long time?

Yes, competition among independent game studios is high and you might have a rough time trying to make it through. Many teams are able to put together a gorgeous presentation, provide impressive demos, and back it all up with a list of successful previous releases.

We met our 101XP colleagues at a gamedev conference in Minsk, Belarus and are now getting ready to release For the People together. We probably got lucky to find the right people — a lot of developers out there fruitlessly look for publishing support for years or are stuck trying to launch their titles themselves.

[h2]To be continued[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/0c0aa27692346ef22fe22edddec5f43cd00b3976.png[/img]

Check out the work done by the guys at Brezg Studio and try on the role of the mayor of a proletarian city in June 2020.

notes.title: Who is Francis River?
notes.content:
Hello, Comrades!

Today we are happy to introduce to you Comrade Francis River, the protagonist of "For the People".

Frank River, a young official, graduated with honors from Corvingtone Institute of Management and National Economy. After joining Com-Union Working Party, he became its active member and served at the Altstad’s department for the past three years. Energetic and ambitious, he wanted to do his best for the people and the country. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/52a835966c4bc33f3eaaa4f89daa30ea477f4bad.jpg[/img]

Thanks to his outstanding education results, he has got into the governmental rotation program and was send to the city of Iron-1 as its new mayor. The youngest mayor in the history of this city, Francis River was 26.

Iron-1 is an industrial city founded in 1888 near wolfram deposits. Back then it was a tiny town but the Orange Revolution turned it into an industrial center with around 50 thousand citizens. The city is divided between people with different political views - Kents and Corvinians. Corvinians are the ruling ones while the Kents are former revolutionaries that now have to live in the current circumstances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35911380/ccfccf1326face7678e141e2ed51f31b7e71183c.png[/img]

Now it’s up to you what Frank will do with the power he’s got. The destiny of Iron-1 and its people is in your hands so choose wisely who to support.

Greetings, Comrade!

The Union of People's Orange Communes needs you! It’s time to travel to Iron-1 and work for the good of the people and the state.

[previewyoutube=76sqB96yRVQ;full][/previewyoutube]
"For the People" is an acute social novel with strategic elements, which invites the player to try on the shoes of a state official. Sort out the townspeople's (sometimes quite unusual) appeals for justice, grant or dismiss requests from subject departments, and untangle a web of political intrigue. Allocate the budget to help the workers or build a new hospital? Support the police or finance an exhibit on the achievements of the agricultural industry? Only you decide!
[list]
[*] Develop a taste for power: play fair or become a corrupt politician;
[*] Think strategically: distribute resources among the residents to earn their trust and increase your own influence;
[*] A constant balancing act: any decision made in-game has its consequences!
[/list]
